section: Citizenship - Articles 5-11; Citizenship Act 1955, acquisition and loss, OCI, CAA 2019
subsections: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11
Terms - NRI, PIO, OCI, Commonwealth citizen, single citizenship
Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions
Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each

accepted.s: Under Article 5 of the Constitution, which of the following was one of the conditions for citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution?
o: Being born outside India to an Indian grandparent
Ordinarily residing in India for five years immediately before commencement
Holding a domicile in India for ten years
Having resided in India for six months after 26 January 1950
accepted.x: Article 5 recognised citizenship at commencement for a person domiciled in India who fulfilled conditions such as birth in India, birth of either parent in India, or ordinary residence in India for five years.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a constitutional condition with nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Article 6 deals with migrants from Pakistan to India.
2. Article 7 deals with persons who migrated to Pakistan after 1 March 1947 but returned to India under a resettlement permit.
3. Article 8 deals with persons of Indian origin residing abroad and registered by an Indian diplomatic or consular representative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Articles 6, 7 and 8 respectively concern migrants from Pakistan, certain returnees from Pakistan, and persons of Indian origin residing abroad who are registered by an Indian diplomatic or consular representative.
accepted.tq: Statement combination using closely related constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person who voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign country would cease to be an Indian citizen under which Article of the Constitution?
accepted.x: Article 9 provides that a person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State cannot be a citizen of India under Articles 5, 6 or 8.
accepted.tq: Article-number discrimination among adjacent provisions.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Article 10 of the Constitution?
o: It provides for continuance of citizenship subject to laws made by Parliament
It empowers diplomatic representatives to register overseas citizens
It prohibits voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship
accepted.x: Article 10 provides for continuance of the rights of citizenship, subject to the provisions of laws made by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Direct provision-to-Article matching.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following powers is expressly assigned to Parliament by Article 11?
o: To regulate acquisition, termination and all other matters relating to citizenship
To decide disputes regarding State boundaries
To register every person born outside India
To determine the electoral college for the President
accepted.x: Article 11 preserves Parliament's power to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
accepted.tq: Who-would-do-this-job approach to identifying the competent constitutional authority.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provisions of Part II of the Constitution primarily deal with citizenship at which point of time?
o: At the time of every general election
At the commencement of the Constitution
At the commencement of the Citizenship Act, 1955
At the commencement of every financial year
accepted.x: Part II deals primarily with persons who were citizens at the commencement of the Constitution; subsequent matters are left to Parliament under Article 11.
accepted.tq: Scope discrimination between constitutional commencement provisions and later legislation.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Articles 5 to 9 of the Constitution came into force on:
accepted.x: Articles 5 to 9 came into force on 26 November 1949, although the Constitution generally commenced on 26 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Date discrimination using constitutionally significant dates.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person who is ordinarily residing outside India but holds an Indian passport is best described as a:
accepted.x: An NRI is an Indian citizen ordinarily residing outside India and holds an Indian passport. PIO and OCI refer to foreign citizens of Indian origin.
accepted.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between NRI, PIO and OCI.
accepted.sec: Terms - NRI, PIO, OCI, Commonwealth citizen, single citizenship  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes a PIO from an NRI?
o: A PIO is an Indian citizen abroad, whereas an NRI is a foreign citizen of Indian origin
A PIO is a foreign citizen of Indian origin, whereas an NRI is an Indian citizen residing abroad
Both PIO and NRI are foreign citizens registered under Section 7A
Both PIO and NRI hold separate citizenship of an Indian State
accepted.x: A PIO is a foreign citizen whose ancestors were Indian nationals, whereas an NRI remains an Indian citizen ordinarily residing outside India.
accepted.tq: Swapped-meaning trap involving two similar citizenship terms.
accepted.sec: Terms - NRI, PIO, OCI, Commonwealth citizen, single citizenship  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about an OCI cardholder:
1. An OCI cardholder is a foreign national of Indian origin registered under the Citizenship Act.
2. An OCI cardholder enjoys a lifelong visa facility.
3. An OCI cardholder can vote in Indian elections as a matter of right.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: OCI cardholders are foreign nationals of Indian origin and enjoy a lifelong visa facility. They cannot vote in Indian elections as OCI cardholders.
accepted.tq: Application of a foreign-citizen status to distinguish permitted and prohibited benefits.
accepted.sec: Terms - NRI, PIO, OCI, Commonwealth citizen, single citizenship  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The concept of single citizenship in India signifies:
o: Citizenship only of the State in which a person is born
Citizenship of both India and every State of residence
Allegiance only to the Union, without separate State citizenship
Citizenship of India only for persons holding government employment
accepted.x: India follows single citizenship, meaning that citizens owe allegiance to the Union and do not possess separate citizenship of individual States.
accepted.tq: Direct recall with reversed-comparison distractors.
accepted.sec: Terms - NRI, PIO, OCI, Commonwealth citizen, single citizenship  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Section of the Citizenship Act, 1955, deals with citizenship by naturalisation?
accepted.x: Section 6 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, deals with acquisition of citizenship by naturalisation.
accepted.tq: Section-number recall using adjacent acquisition provisions as distractors.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Section)
a. Section 3
b. Section 4
c. Section 5
d. Section 7
List-II (Provision)
i. Citizenship by descent
ii. Citizenship by incorporation of territory
iii. Citizenship by birth
iv. Citizenship by registration

Codes:
accepted.x: Section 3 concerns citizenship by birth, Section 4 by descent, Section 5 by registration, and Section 7 by incorporation of territory.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure section-provision pair and complete the code.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Section 9 deals with termination of citizenship, whereas Section 10 deals with deprivation of citizenship. Section 8 concerns renunciation and Section 7A concerns OCI cardholders.
accepted.tq: Find one wrong section-provision pair among adjacent provisions.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 14A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, provides for:
o: The merger of PIO and OCI cards
The National Register of Indian Citizens and a national identity card
accepted.x: Section 14A provides for the National Register of Indian Citizens and the issue of a national identity card.
accepted.tq: Exact provision-to-section recall with nearby citizenship topics as distractors.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes renunciation of citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
o: It is made by declaration, and minor children also lose citizenship but may resume it within one year of attaining majority
It can be ordered only by a State Government
It applies only to citizens by naturalisation
It occurs automatically whenever a person resides abroad for five years
accepted.x: Renunciation is effected by declaration. Minor children of the person renouncing citizenship also lose citizenship, but they may resume it within one year after attaining majority.
accepted.tq: Scenario-based testing of the legal consequence and exception attached to renunciation.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country. Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, this ordinarily results in:
o: Deprivation by the Central Government after inquiry in every case
Conversion into OCI status without any further process
accepted.x: Termination of Indian citizenship occurs automatically when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country. This is distinct from renunciation and deprivation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish automatic termination from discretionary deprivation and voluntary renunciation.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Deprivation of citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955, may be ordered by the Central Government in respect of citizens who acquired citizenship by:
o: Residence in India for five years
Naturalisation, registration or under Article 5(c), subject to the prescribed grounds
accepted.x: Deprivation by the Central Government applies only to citizens by naturalisation, registration or Article 5(c), and may be based on grounds such as fraud, disloyalty or helping an enemy during war.
accepted.tq: Authority-and-eligibility trap involving the power of the Central Government.
accepted.sec: Sections of the Citizenship Act 1955 - provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1986, changed the requirement for citizenship by birth by providing that, for births from 1 July 1987:
o: The person must have resided in India for six months
The person must hold an OCI card
At least one parent must be an Indian citizen
Both parents must be Indian citizens
accepted.x: The 1986 amendment provided that citizenship by birth for persons born from 1 July 1987 required at least one parent to be an Indian citizen.
accepted.tq: Date-and-condition pairing using a changed eligibility threshold.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003:
1. It introduced the OCI scheme.
2. It added Section 14A relating to the National Register of Indian Citizens.
3. From 3 December 2004, the other parent was required not to be an illegal migrant for the relevant citizenship-by-birth condition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2003 amendment introduced OCI, added Section 14A, and from 3 December 2004 required the other parent not to be an illegal migrant for the relevant birth-based citizenship condition.
accepted.tq: Multi-statement testing of one amendment’s date, institution and eligibility change.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which amendment widened the OCI scheme?
accepted.x: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005, widened the OCI scheme. The 2003 amendment introduced OCI, while the 2015 amendment merged PIO and OCI cards.
accepted.tq: Distinguish successive amendments dealing with the same OCI subject.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Citizenship Amendments in chronological order:
A. Merger of PIO and OCI cards
B. Introduction of OCI and addition of Section 14A
C. Widening of the OCI scheme
D. Change in citizenship by birth requiring one parent to be an Indian citizen for births from 1 July 1987
accepted.x: The relevant sequence is the 1986 amendment, the 2003 amendment, the 2005 amendment and the 2015 amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last amendments, then place the two intermediate changes.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, provided a pathway to citizenship for members of six communities originating from:
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment created a pathway to citizenship for members of six specified communities from three countries.
accepted.tq: Split the option by comparing the number of communities with the number of countries.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the year 2008 is correct in the context of the Citizenship Act amendments listed?
o: The Citizenship Act was amended in 2008 to introduce OCI
No amendment was made to the Citizenship Act in 2008
The Citizenship Act was amended in 2008 to add Section 14A
The Citizenship Act was amended in 2008 to merge PIO and OCI cards
accepted.x: No amendment was made to the Citizenship Act in 2008. OCI was introduced in 2003, Section 14A was added in 2003, and the PIO-OCI merger occurred in 2015.
accepted.tq: Negative year discrimination against nearby amendment years.
accepted.sec: Citizenship (Amendment) Acts 1986, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 - change made by each  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a right or eligibility restricted to citizens of India rather than being generally available to all persons?
o: Freedom of speech and expression under Article 19
Protection of life and personal liberty
Protection against arbitrary deprivation of property
accepted.x: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are citizen-specific provisions. The right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 is therefore available only to citizens.
accepted.tq: Compare citizen-only rights with rights available to persons generally.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following offices may be held by a naturalised citizen of India?
o: Only the office of Attorney-General, but not President
Only the office of Governor, but not President
No constitutional office under any circumstance
accepted.x: A naturalised citizen can become the President of India, subject to fulfilling the constitutional qualifications for the office.
accepted.tq: Exception testing against the common but incorrect assumption that only citizens by birth may hold the office.
accepted.sec: Articles 5-11 and Part II - citizens at commencement, Article 10, Article 11  [APPSC]
